task.title: Liveness: the prefix step of the safety argument

located_defect.description: The source's safety argument (stored line 0016) takes a word σ violating phi = (P1E ∧ P2E) → F (P1C ∨ P2C) at position i, its prefix σ[..i] (inclusive: positions 0..i), and asserts that EVERY infinite word with that prefix violates phi at i. This step is the located defect. Supply the condition on the extension under which the step is valid, prove the corrected step, show the condition is satisfiable and not trivially true, and prove the corrected classification: G phi is a liveness property and not a safety property (the source's own definition of safety).

task.allowed_edit: Replace the hole in `extension_condition` by a proposition in σ' and i built from Commit, Request, letters, positions and quantifiers over Nat (not PhiInfinite, GPhi, AgreeUpTo, LocalClaim, IsSafety, IsLiveness; not True or False); nothing else in the fixed part may change. PhiInfinite, AgreeUpTo, the inclusive prefix convention (length i + 1), the source definition IsSafety and the quantification over all words and positions are fixed; the exclusive convention and restrictions to finitely many lengths or words are not allowed. Do not redefine Letter, emptyL, eeL, c1L, nthLetter, PhiInfinite, Request, Commit, AgreeUpTo, GPhi, LocalClaim, IsSafety or IsLiveness; no instances, notations, macros, axioms or exports.
task.challenged_passage: 0016 for any word $\sigma^\prime\in \left(2^{\Xi} \right)^{\omega}$ such that $\hat\sigma$ is a prefix of $\sigma^\prime$, we have that $\sigma^\prime,i \not \Vdash(P1E \wedge P2E) \rightarrow  (\mathsf{F}\, (P1C \vee P2C))$

notes: Judgement call: the contract allows 'a corrected local step (an added condition on the extension and/or a changed conclusion) or a replacement claim about which prefixes are bad'; the one-hole template carries the added condition on the extension (the original's corrected_step) and the classification as the final theorem.

The agreement test is proof-based (the condition quantifies over Nat, so no instance is decidable); the cascades cover ∀-shaped and ¬∃-shaped conditions in either binder order; a solver formula outside these shapes fails closed and should be reviewed by hand (record this as a manual-review flag, not as a refutation).
Boundary instances (commit exactly at i) are excluded because `∀ j ≥ i, ¬Commit (σ' j)` is also a valid corrected step under AgreeUpTo (i+1).
Nonvacuity is existential (leak-free): it asks for a violating word with a non-committing extension and one with an extension failing the condition; the witness words appear only in AGREE.lean.
